notes:
{良|よ}い is an i-adjective meaning "good." Its irregular alternative ⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧ is the ordinary form in everyday speech.

USAGE:
- よい is the more formal, written, and older-sounding form; ⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧ dominates conversation
- よい persists in set phrases and greetings: よい⟦お{年|とし}→年：00486_toshi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ (have a good new year), ⟦{仲|なか}→仲：09513_naka⟧よく (on good terms)
- Whichever dictionary form is used, everything else conjugates from よ-, never い-

FORMS:
- Dictionary: よい or ⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧ (いい is more casual)
- Negative: よくない (NOT いくない)
- Past: よかった (NOT いかった)
- Adverb: よく (well, often)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- 〜てもよい / 〜ても⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧: may ~, it's okay to ~
- 〜ばよかった: should have ~ (regret)
- 〜なくても⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧: don't have to ~
